chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who blinded an eye of a woman, he said: If they so desire, they can blind his eye and pay him a quarter of the wergild; and if she so desires, she can take the quarter of the wergild.
And he said regarding a woman who blinded an eye of a man: If he so desires, he can blind her eye, or else he takes the wergild for his eye.

key_terms.فَقَأَ: to blind or puncture an eye

ai.seo_question: What are the rules of qisas and diya for eye injuries between men and women in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of 'equal retaliation' (ta'adul) in qisas, highlighting the jurisprudential nuance that while the physical injury is identical, the financial compensation (diya) differs due to the general rule that a woman's diya is half that of a man's. It demonstrates the flexibility in Shia fiqh where the injured party retains the option to choose between exact physical retribution or accepting the corresponding monetary value, reflecting the balance between justice and compensation in personal injury cases.
